subject: Measurement Invariance: freely estimate latent means

messages.author: 5361e059e0de425b
messages.subject: Measurement Invariance: freely estimate latent means
parts:
Hello,

I'm doing a measurement invariance using lavaan. 

Based on my model comparison tests, I need to freely estimate a latent mean. Can someone please tell me the syntax that freely estimates latent means 

Thank you

messages.author: b207b6a270f65efc
messages.subject: Re: Measurement Invariance: freely estimate latent means
parts:
Hi
if you are familiar with lavaan language, a simple way to do that is to set the meanstructure argument to TRUE, a meanstructure is added to the model. this example is from lavaan page.
> fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939,
+ meanstructure = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: Measurement Invariance: freely estimate latent means
parts: No, you're right--constraints on the latent means are not part of invariance testing--that's more like an analog of a t-test or one-way ANOVA. For invariance testing, typically one mean is fixed to zero for reference, and any others are freely estimated, though you can also fix the reference through indicator intercepts if you'd rather.

parts: I need to freely estimate a latent mean. Can someone please tell me the syntax that freely estimates latent means

Means are intercepts of variables without predictors.  You set them free using the same syntax as for intercepts:

https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/means.html

messages.author: 5361e059e0de425b
messages.subject: Re: Measurement Invariance: freely estimate latent means
parts:
Sorry all for the confusing question.

What I should have asked was syntax to freely estimate the factor means. 
I completed strict invariance. 
Some best practices suggest that I can move from constraining residuals variances to constraining factor means.  I've added the syntax that I am currently using.

fit7 <- sem(model1, data = fgcs, std.lv = TRUE, test = "satorra.bentler", missing = "listwise", estimator = "MLM", group = "Q28a", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals", "means"), 
            group.partial = c("Q8e ~1"))

To freely estimate factor means I am doing the following:
NetFri ~ 1 where NetFri is my latent variable.
I don't believe this is the correct approach but it was my best guess. 

Perhaps the problem could be that NetFri ~ 1 is not the correct syntax for factor means?

Also, I noticed, when using lavTestScore(fit7, epc = TRUE), there are 'NA' in parts of my latent variables
